claims.text: Adding 5 wt% tungsten will improve the high-temperature mechanical capability of refractory high-entropy alloys.
Adding 5 wt% tungsten will limit alloy density.
Adding 5 wt% tungsten will preserve room-temperature performance.
The intervention is applicable to refractory high-entropy alloys in the as-cast state.
The proposed effect will hold above 1000°C for 100 hours under a load of 100 MPa.
Tungsten addition will produce solid-solution strengthening.
Tungsten addition will precipitate tungsten-rich phases.
Prior studies on refractory metals support the proposed tungsten alloying effects.
Alloying and solid-solution strengthening from tungsten will enhance high-temperature mechanical properties.
At 1000°C, adding 5 wt% tungsten will increase yield strength by 150 MPa relative to the tungsten-free baseline.
The tungsten-free baseline has a yield strength of 1000 MPa at 1000°C.
The proposed operating boundary is 900–1100°C and 50–150 MPa.
The temperature range of 900–1100°C is relevant to jet-turbine applications.
The loading range of 50–150 MPa covers the expected operational range for jet-turbine applications.
The yield-strength improvement may vary with the specific refractory-alloy composition and processing conditions.
A measured yield strength below 1150 MPa for the tungsten-modified alloy at 1000°C would falsify the predicted strength improvement.

contradictions.description: The conditions state that the effect holds above 1000°C, whereas the quantified prediction is made at exactly 1000°C and the stated boundary extends down to 900°C.
